text:
Jordan: Heads-up — saw a sustained queue-depth spike in ap-southeast-1 between ~02:10–03:05 UTC. Grafana headroom-by-pool panel showed oscillation (scale up -> scale down -> scale up). Burst-capacity costs spiked ~18% for that hour.
Maria: Thanks, any panels/queries you pulled? can you paste the PromQL?
Jordan: Paste below. Screenshot linked: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abc123/headroom-by-pool (private)
```
# queue depth by pool/region
sum by(pool, region) (inference_queue_depth{region="ap-southeast-1"})

# 5m max GPU saturation to avoid transient spikes
max_over_time(gpu_pool_saturation{region="ap-southeast-1"}[5m])
```
Kevin: Two quick thoughts — alerting + autoscaler hysteresis. The current alert is firing on `inference_queue_depth > 50` instantly; that causes ops to react and the autoscaler to overshoot. We should switch to a smoothed expression and `for: 10m`, or use `increase(...[5m])` to detect growing queues rather than transient blips.
Olivia: Also noticed batch-size distribution skew in the logs — more tiny batches which kills throughput on the GPU. PromQL for average batch size:
```
(rate(batch_size_sum[5m])[5m]) / (rate(batch_size_count[5m])[5m])
```
The 95th percentile dropped from ~12->3 during the spike. Small batches = less amortized kernel work -> saturation.
Jordan: Good catch. That explains why saturation persisted despite new replicas: throughput per-GPU was low.
Kevin: Proposal:
- Change alert to `max_over_time(inference_queue_depth[10m]) > 40` with `for: 8m` to avoid flapping.
- Replace instant scale-down with cooldown: `scale_down_delay: 600s` and `min_replicas` bump by 1 for the ap-southeast pools during peak hours.
- Add batch-size SLO panel and an alert on `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_processing_time_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool)) > 0.25` to catch slow-processing outliers.
Maria: 👍 on the smoothing. For alert grouping, include `by(pool,region)` so we don't blow up paging across many pools. Also, change notification to #eng-infra-oncall only for first page, escalate to #eng-sre if persists 20m.
Olivia: Another mitigation: route small-batch traffic to a special pool tuned for low-latency (smaller batch threshold). That reduces cross-pool interference. Can we add a routing rule in the control plane? @opsbot can create an RFC?
opsbot: RFC created: RFC-2026-58 "small-batch routing rule for ap-southeast-1" (link: https://rfc.redwood/internal/RFC-2026-58).
sre-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-114 created for the spike; attaching logs and the Grafana dashboard snapshot.
Jordan: I'm going to prototype the alert change and cooldown adjustments in staging today, then roll to ap-southeast during our maintenance window tonight.
Kevin: When we roll, please also enable a temporary quota to prevent runaway burst-capacity billing (cap = +1 replica over baseline) and track cost delta.
Maria: I can update the dashboard: add batch-size p95 panel, and a headroom-smoothing overlay using `avg_over_time(gpu_pool_headroom[10m])`.
Olivia: I'll draft routing config and a quick smoke-test plan (5m at a time).
Jordan: Action items:
• Jordan — change alert and autoscaler cooldown in staging (today)
• Maria — add p95 batch-size and headroom-smoothing panels (today)
• Olivia — RFC and routing config + smoke test plan (this afternoon)
• Kevin — quota patch for burst-capacity during rollout (tomorrow)
• opsbot/sre-bot — keep INC-2026-114 updated and attach cost metrics

Jordan: Thanks all. If the staging run looks good I'll request the maintenance window and post the timeline here. :thumbsup:
